sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: ELISA-based internalization assay (L1): HA-tagged hIP is detected on the cell surface and undergoes cicaprost-stimulated internalization, confirming surface display and ligand-driven trafficking. Functional coupling not directly measured in the tagged construct alone.
sites.rationale: PTGIR is a GPCR with no signal peptide; residues 1–17 form the extracellular N-terminus and TM1 begins at residue 18. The HA tag on the full-length receptor must reside at the N-terminal prepend (insert_after_residue=0, residue_after=M) because that is the only extracellular terminus available. Python verification confirms seq[0]='M' and seq[17]='A' (TM1 start), placing 17 extracellular residues between the tag and TM1—ample space for a ~15–23 aa insert. L4 (BRIL at N-terminus of WT IP) independently validates N-terminal fusion tolerance in a full-length membrane-anchored context. HA-tagged full-length human IP receptor (hIP/hPTGIR) stably expressed in HEK293 cells (HEK.hIP clonal line); no residue is named in any ledger clip. PTGIR has no signal peptide (topology residues 1–17 are extracellular); the N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus of this GPCR, so the prepend junction (position 0, before M1) is the only location consistent with an extracellular HA tag. L4 independently confirms N-terminal tagging: a BRIL tag was fused to the N-terminus of WT full-length IP receptor for cryo-EM structural studies of IP–Gs complexes.

sources.claim: To begin with, we used an ELISA-based internalization assay to measure net changes in cell surface expression of hemagglutinin (HA)-tagged hIPs in response to cicaprost stimulation of HEK.hIP cells, a previously characterized clonal cell line [15,17] .

literature_notes: L2 and L3 describe the same pcDNA5-HA-hPTGIR construct used for mutagenesis studies; they add no positional or functional information beyond what L1 already establishes and are therefore not promoted to separate sites. L4 (BRIL N-terminal fusion) corroborates the same N-terminal junction and is noted in the rationale of the single site rather than listed separately, because it pins the identical junction (position 0). L5 (LgBiT at C-terminus) is recorded in other_positions because the C-terminus of PTGIR is intracellular (residues 296–386). No ledger line names a residue within any extracellular loop (ECL1 74–93, ECL2 160–181, ECL3 261–274), so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: LgBiT fused to the C-terminus of full-length IP receptor (NanoBiT tethering strategy); residue 386 (C) is within the intracellular C-terminal tail (topology 296–386), so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface-accessible site.
